items.text: Silent Machine
Hallway, Foundation

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: I'm terribly sorry, Timekeeper. We've failed our mission. I should have done something sooner …
This wasn't your fault, Sonetto.
I'm afraid it was completely unavoidable.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: No, no need to comfort me, Timekeeper. I'm prepared to take full responsibility.

items.speaker: Messenger
items.text: Sonetto!

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: … Yes!

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Well, I'm going in.
Sonetto disappears through the door to the interrogation room.

items.speaker: X
items.text: Ah, I should have expected we'd fall into some trouble when we returned to the Foundation.

items.speaker: X
items.text: Seems like I'm not cut out for field missions.
Is that really the story you're going with?

items.speaker: X
items.text: What? We haven't even entered the interrogation room, and you're already starting to question me?
Don't change the subject, Mr. X.

items.speaker: X
items.text: Fine. But before you begin, let me ask first …

items.speaker: X
items.text: What makes you think I did anything?
Your absence at the scene was noted. Convenient, even—
items.edge_label: きみはあの時、現場にいなかった

items.speaker: X
items.text: I was just playing games with the kids. You read the report.

items.speaker: X
items.text: I'm sure you'll find they all passed the Lie Detector test that was administered, verifying my whereabouts at the time.
Sound of gears was heard at the crime scene.
items.edge_label: 現場で歯車の音がした

items.speaker: X
items.text: And I'm sure you also read that the report concluded that there was a loose part on the sign. As for gears, come on, it's New York. That could have been anything!
It's easy to fake an accident with Goldberg Machine.
items.edge_label:
ゴールドバーグ・マシンを使えば
容易に事故を装える

items.speaker: X
items.text: All of life is a Rube Goldberg machine. The only question is the outcome, and the initial point.

items.speaker: X
items.text: But you're asking "Did I make it." If I did, where was its fulcrum? There wasn't any trace of a machine at the scene.
Thoughts begin to race.
Ultimately, X is the common feature of every Goldberg apparatus …
From Regulus's firework lighting cue.
To Sophie's marble launching spring.
Human action is the initial point for every mechanical device. The participants themselves are a part of the experiment. Their behavior, their actions, engineered as a part of the machine.
Stable, controllable, and able to follow instructions.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Via Pellar!
Your fulcrum was a person.
You used her. You used Sonetto.
items.edge_label: きみはソネットを利用した

items.speaker: X
items.text: I don't know what you could possibly mean.

items.speaker: X
items.text: We both know I wasn't there. So how could I have controlled Ms. Sonetto's actions?

items.speaker: X
items.text: Are you trying to say that Ms. Sonetto acted as my accomplice?

items.speaker: X
items.text: That's a very serious accusation, wouldn't you say?
… You!

items.speaker: Messenger
items.text: Vertin!

items.speaker: X
items.text: Tsk, they're calling you, Vertin.

items.speaker: X
items.text: Maybe we can talk more after this?
Interrogation Room

items.speaker: Inquisitor
items.text: So, do you have any additional information to add about the incident? Anything that could help would be welcome, Timekeeper.

items.speaker: Inquisitor
items.text: Please answer honestly.
Silence.
At first, the choice to speak up would have only implicated one person.
But that is no longer the case.
I have shared all the information I know.
items.edge_label: …知ってることは全て話しました

items.speaker: Inquisitor
items.text: I understand. Thank you for your cooperation.
The wait for the verdict drags on, a sword hanging over the heads of two friends, dangling on a thread.
Finally …

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Timekeeper! Great! I've been looking for you!

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: I'm to inform you that the Foundation has dismissed their investigation.
Dismissed?

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: The results from the crime scene found no trace of unexpected arcane activity. The case has been officially ruled an accident.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Still, I'm planning on staying late at the Foundation, so I can volunteer for the very next mission. I must rectify this blot on our record!

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Are you leaving?
Yes. I have something to take care of.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Oh, alright. Well … See you soon.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: By the way, it seems like the patent acquisition was terminated after Mr. Wilson's accident. So, it seems the price of the drug will remain $1!
Could this truly have been God's will?
Or perhaps it was there a Devil in the machine?

items.speaker: X
items.text: You look angry.
Did you know—Did you see this coming?

items.speaker: X
items.text: You're overestimating my skills, Ms. Vertin.

items.speaker: X
items.text: Arcanists are good with intuitive insight, and humans are good with logic-based deduction.

items.speaker: X
items.text: When the two compete against each other, they might turn a blind eye to the absurdity and chaos that is the world and what happens to certain people in it.

items.speaker: X
items.text: Vertin, I am sorry about the accident.

items.speaker: X
items.text: But "the rain falls on the just and the unjust alike," isn't that what they say?

items.speaker: X
items.text: Arcanists and humans, the poor and the rich. As long as we all walk this earth, we're all the same.

items.speaker: X
items.text: That's just how the world works.
So, are we all just cogs in the machine to you?
items.edge_label:
わたしたちも、
きみの装置の一部だと？

items.speaker: X
items.text: When the marble is set, it doesn't really matter who triggers the spring. Its flight and its target will always be the same.

items.speaker: X
items.text: In fact, when you consider the mechanistic nature of reality, we're all cogs of one kind or another.
But you used your friend. My friend.
items.edge_label: でも、きみは仲間を利用した

items.text: You used her.

items.speaker: X
items.text: That's why you're upset? … Hm, well, I understand.

items.speaker: X
items.text: Don't worry … I promise you won't see anymore "devices that pose safety risks" in the laboratory after this.
X turns to leave, but stops again.

items.speaker: X
items.text: —Oh, now that their investigation is over, would you mind if I took some of these letters off your hands?
The mechanical expert smiles, waving the documents back at her before disappearing through the laboratory doorway.
The fireplace burns low and quiet.

items.speaker: X
items.text: "… In conclusion, Researcher X's study on mechanical devices poses significant safety risks …"

items.speaker: X
items.text: "Which, through unintended consequences, might result in damages, including but not limited to burns, collisions, disabilities, death, etc."
X takes a sip of his coffee, marveling with pride at the words as he raises the letter into the air.

items.speaker: X
items.text: A marvelous insight. These machines certainly have their dangers.

items.speaker: X
items.text: Burning ... That certainly is a risk.
X taps the edge of his cup, beginning a series of outrageous mechanical movements, as Mesmer's stack of complaints is pulled one by one from his desk and funneled into the fireplace.
Where they turn to ash, leaving not a single trace.
THE END
